clarification_questions.question: What goes wrong today with the water content in the petroleum line, and what decision would real-time water data drive?
clarification_questions.why: Determines whether an online MIR ATR sensor is needed at all or whether a simpler or periodic method answers the need.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Pain and decision unknown; proceed only with lab screening to establish whether online measurement is justified.

clarification_questions.question: What water content level must be measured (ppm or %), and over what range?
clarification_questions.why: The level decides whether MIR ATR sensitivity and the ATR probe are suitable, since water absorbs strongly in the mid-IR.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Level unknown; lab screening establishes whether the required level is ppm or % level before any probe choice.

clarification_questions.question: Is the petroleum a clear, turbid or opaque liquid, and does it contain solids, emulsions or free water droplets?
clarification_questions.why: Determines whether ATR contact with the liquid is representative and whether scattering or droplets bias the signal.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Optical state unknown; assume a liquid that must be checked for emulsion or droplet effects in lab screening.

clarification_questions.question: What are the operating temperature, pressure and fouling conditions of the line, and does the water content vary in time or with stream composition?
clarification_questions.why: Temperature and fouling affect ATR contact, probe materials and calibration stability.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Operating conditions unknown; the probe and calibration cannot be specified until they are supplied.

clarification_questions.question: What is the link length, routing and fiber type of the existing silica cable, and what is its measured or specified transmission in the MIR region?
clarification_questions.why: Silica fibers cannot carry mid-IR light, so the reuse of this cable decides whether MIR ATR is possible at all; the fiber specification in the MIR region must be checked.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Silica cable assumed unsuitable for MIR until the fiber specification is checked; MIR needs chalcogenide, polycrystalline or hollow-waveguide fibers.

clarification_questions.question: What is the current reference lab method for water content, and what accuracy does it achieve?
clarification_questions.why: Needed to compare the MIR ATR result against an accepted reference over time-aligned samples.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Reference method unknown; a comparison design cannot be set up until it is named.

clarification_questions.question: What accuracy, response time and budget are required for the water measurement?
clarification_questions.why: Defines whether a full MIR system, a simpler method or a periodic lab check is proportionate.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Requirements unknown; proceed with lab screening and defer any sensor specification.

flags_before_revision.detail: overstated: The claim says MIR fiber probes 'need' chalcogenide or polycrystalline silver halide fibers. S04 p.1 says these materials have sufficient mid-IR transmittance, not that they are required. S02 p.6 also lists other IR fibers (hollow glass waveguides, indium fluoride, zirconium fluoride), so the requirement is overstated. Fix: Say that chalcogenide or polycrystalline silver halide fibers are one option for mid-IR transmission, citing S04 p.1, and note that other mid-IR fiber types exist per S02 p.6.

not_supported: DOCX §3 contains only general guidance about not giving guarantees and about treating a published application as a reason to test. It does not state that 'the fiber link is contradicted'. Fix: Remove the claim about the fiber link being contradicted. Keep only the supported point that no approval or guarantee can be given without measurements.

not_supported: S01 p.10 covers ATR fiber probes, NIR diffuse reflection and diode-array instruments. It says nothing about crude grade or composition changes invalidating a calibration. Fix: Cite a source that discusses calibration transfer or sample-composition effects, or present the calibration risk as a general assumption to be tested rather than sourced.

not_supported: The cited table rows give only the ATR optical path (1-6 um) and qualitative ratings. Nothing on the cited pages mentions fouling or droplets biasing ATR readings. Fix: Keep the sourced point that the ATR optical path is about 1-6 um, and state fouling or droplet effects as an untested assumption to check in the feasibility plan.

rule_hints: nominal_range_not_instrument_range: A nominal method range is not the usable range of a specific instrument, fiber or probe. [DOCX §3; DOCX §5]

fiber_limits_wavelength: The fiber determines which wavelengths reach the probe. Silica fibers transmit up to about 2.4 um and cannot carry mid-IR; mid-IR needs chalcogenide, polycrystalline or hollow-waveguide fibers. [S02 p.6; S04 p.1; DOCX §5]
remote_measurement_nir_silica: NIR works with standard glass optics and silica fibers, which suits remote online measurement; robust silica cables of 100-300 m exist. [S01 p.5; S02 p.7]
do_not_invent: Do not invent measured results, accuracy, detection limits, response times, fiber lengths, product codes or prices, client facts, or guarantees. [DOCX §3]
insufficient_information_is_valid: If the known facts cannot justify a method choice, say so, ask the deciding questions and propose the next step. [DOCX §3]
